title: Singh's Royal Butter Chicken
description: A rich, velvety butter chicken made from scratch with our family's signature recipe. Tandoori-marinated chicken is simmered in a silky tomato-onion gravy finished with butter, cream, honey, and kasuri methi.
steps: Wash and pat the chicken dry.
Combine the chicken with the ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and a little salt. Marinate for 3-4 hours.
Mix together all the ingredients for the second marination until smooth.
Coat the chicken thoroughly and marinate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Cook the chicken in a tandoor, oven, grill, or air fryer until about 90% cooked. Set aside.

Meanwhile, combine the tomatoes, onions, garlic, ginger, black peppercorns, cloves, cinnamon, cumin seeds, coriander powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, green chilies, green cardamom, and chicken masala in a large pot.
Add enough water to cover everything and bring to a boil.
Cook for about 30 minutes, or until the onions and tomatoes become completely soft.
Allow the mixture to cool slightly, then blend until completely smooth.
Pass the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve for an ultra-silky restaurant-style texture.
Heat the butter, desi ghee, and olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan.
Add the coriander powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, and kasuri methi. Cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the strained gravy and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the honey and tomato ketchup and mix well.
Add the cooked tandoori chicken and simmer for 5-7 minutes so the chicken absorbs the gravy.
Pour in the heavy cream and continue cooking over low heat for another 5-10 minutes until the curry becomes rich, glossy, and velvety.
Finish with another pinch of freshly crushed kasuri methi.
Garnish with a swirl of fresh cream, a small cube of butter, and a light sprinkle of kasuri methi before serving.
notes: Chicken thighs remain much juicier than breast meat and are recommended for this recipe.
Straining the gravy is essential for achieving a smooth, restaurant-style butter chicken.
For an even deeper flavor, let the finished curry simmer gently for an additional 20-30 minutes on very low heat.
Do not boil the curry after adding the cream; keep it at a gentle simmer to prevent splitting.
The small amount of honey and ketchup balances the natural acidity of the tomatoes without making the curry noticeably sweet.
This butter chicken pairs beautifully with butter naan, garlic naan, tandoori roti, laccha paratha, or jeera rice.
